conviction_note: Nothing company-specific and unpriced was found; the one large new fact (a 85-90bp rise in 5-10yr Treasuries plus a 25bp Fed hike inside Q3, hitting a $407M AFS book and $1.6B of time deposits) is market-wide and partly in a bank tape that fell ~10% in a month, so p_up sits at 52 and the scaled number is near zero while the findings sum to +0.95 on small, mostly disclosed positives (sub-debt redemption, buyback pace, possible dividend raise, REO resolution).
bar: EPS $0.57 from two agreeing sources: Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/RBB, read 2026-10-19) and Zacks via Nasdaq ($0.57, revenue $34.07M, estimate revised -0.34% in 30 days; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/rbb-rbb-earnings-expected-grow-should-you-buy). Q2 2026 actual was $0.59 with a $0 provision (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001499422/000143774926023874/ex_970512.htm). No company EPS guidance; expenses guided $18-19M at the high end, tax rate ~28%.
positioning_check: Short interest 530,405 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 3.36% of float, 4.7 days to cover, down 10.0% from 589,131 on 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RBB/short-interest/, read 2026-10-19). Not crowded; no squeeze mechanism either way. No option chain (baseline: empty_chain), so no skew. Tape: spot 25.54, -4.52% over 20d, -8.5% from the 52w high, 20d realised vol 13%, avg volume 83k shares (~$2.1M/day). FJ Capital, a 9.96% holder a year ago, reported 0% as of 2026-06-30 (13G/A), so the bank-specialist seller is finished.

findings.finding: Q3 was a rate-shock quarter the Q2 release could not have reflected: the 10yr par yield rose from 4.44% (2026-06-30) to 5.29% (2026-09-30) and the 5yr from 4.19% to 5.09% (Treasury), and the FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0); RBB carried $407.2M of AFS securities with a $14.6M AOCI loss at 6/30 and $1.61B of time deposits, so the print likely shows a larger AOCI loss (roughly $10M after tax, ~$0.60/share or ~2% of the $27.23 TBV, my arithmetic at ~4yr duration) and a cost-of-funds direction that turns up into Q4 as ~$1.5B of CDs reprice, against the CFO's July view that deposit costs would be 'the same or slightly improved'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RBB's Q2 2026 print (NIM -9bp q/q to 3.06%) moved -0.41%; Jan 2026 -0.74%; the name has not sold NIM compression hard. Baseline median abs move 1.85%, 5 of 7 up.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate move is public and the bank index reportedly fell ~9.7% in the month into earnings (secondary source), but RBB itself is only -4.5% over 20 days and -0.6% over 5, with 13% realised vol and an empty option chain: no one has repriced this specific name for its own TBV hit or its CD-heavy funding (time deposits ~47% of deposits). If it were priced, the 20d drift would track the index and the stock would not sit 6% above its July print level.
findings.independence: Proxy / macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. Three separate documents point the same way: the FOMC statement (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm, 2026-09-16), the Treasury par curve, and RBB's own 10-Q for the AFS and time-deposit balances (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001499422/000143774926026563/rbb20260630_10q.htm, filed 2026-08-07). Offsetting: Regions printed NIM +2bp q/q on 2026-10-16 with hedges, so not every bank compressed.

findings.finding: RBB redeemed $40M of its $120M subordinated notes on 2026-07-01, the day the coupon reset to 7.02%; the remaining $80M costs ~$1.4M/quarter, so Q3 carries ~$0.7M less sub-debt interest than Q2 (about 7bp of NIM gross, ~3bp net of the yield forgone on the cash), the first full quarter after the 9bp q/q NIM drop that the April repricing caused.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2026 repricing (NIM 3.15% -> 3.06%) was reported 2026-07-20 and the stock moved -0.41%; a partial reversal is a small positive on a line the stock has barely traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside what the company already disclosed on 2026-07-20, so mostly priced; consensus EPS of $0.57 sits below Q2's $0.59 despite it, which suggests the Street has netted it against higher funding costs rather than ignored it. Filed small because it is a disclosed, mechanical item.
findings.independence: Same document as the Q2 call commentary (CFO Hopkins: retiring part of the sub-debt should recover some margin, https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026, 2026-07-21). One source, one fact.

findings.finding: The board is actively considering a dividend increase: CFO Lynn Hopkins said on the Q2 call that raising the quarterly dividend 'is something we would consider' now that capital actions are in place and the board is 'looking at it'; the dividend has been $0.16 since the January 2023 declaration (ex-date 2023-01-27, raised from $0.14), and the Q3 release is the next scheduled declaration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last raise (to $0.16, with the Q4 2022 print in January 2023) is outside the baseline window; the baseline carries no dividend-driven reaction. Yield at spot is 2.5%; a raise to $0.18 would add ~0.3pt of yield.
findings.why_not_priced: No analyst note since July mentions a raise and the five-analyst consensus is Neutral at $28.50 (https://www.investing.com/equities/rbb-bancorp-consensus-estimates); the raise is a probability (I put it near 30% for this print versus the January declaration), not a fact, and the size reflects that.
findings.independence: Dividend history from FullRatio (https://fullratio.com/stocks/nasdaq-rbb/dividend) and Digrin (https://digrin.com/stocks/detail/RBB/) agree on $0.14 -> $0.16 at the 2023-01-27 ex-date; the Q1 and Q2 2026 releases declared $0.16 again.

findings.finding: The buyback kept running after quarter end: the 10-Q cover shows 16,915,964 shares outstanding at 2026-07-31 against 16,985,919 at 2026-06-30, so ~70,000 shares (0.4% of the company, ~$1.9M at ~$27) were retired in July alone, a faster pace than Q2's 180,576 shares for $4.47M, and at 0.94x the $27.23 TBV it is accretive; the June 2026 plan of up to 1,000,000 shares was largely unused at 6/30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline turned on buyback pace; the 2026-04-20 print (+5.45%) came with the share count falling, the 2026-07-20 print (-0.41%) likewise, so this line alone has not moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The cover-page count is a footnote nobody aggregates; consensus EPS of $0.57 was revised down 0.34% in 30 days, not up for a lower share count. It is worth about half a cent of EPS per quarter, hence the small size.
findings.independence: CFO Hopkins on the Q2 call: 'our appetite is healthy' and the company will 'pay attention to opportunities relative to our stock price' (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026, 2026-07-21). Shares the 10-Q with the AFS/time-deposit figures in finding 1 but rests on a different number.

findings.finding: The largest problem asset, a $19.4M credit moved to REO, was targeted for resolution 'in the second half of this year' (CFO Hopkins, Q2 call: 'we would be looking for a resolution... but appreciate it is still complicated', needs 'the right buyer'); NPAs were $43.6M at 6/30 after a $5.3M (10.8%) q/q fall, NPLs $23.8M (0.72% of loans), allowance/NPLs 183.8%, Q2 OREO result a $221k loss; a Q3 sale at carrying value would cut NPAs by ~45%, a write-down on sale is the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit is the line this stock trades on: 2025-10-20 +6.76% and 2026-04-20 +5.45% came with NPA declines (Q1 2026 NPLs fell from 1.34% to 0.72% by Q2), while the Q2 2026 print with NPAs -10.8% moved only -0.41%, so a decline alone is not enough; a resolution of the single largest asset is a different order of magnitude.
findings.why_not_priced: No 8-K, release or news item between 2026-07-21 and today reports a sale (the only 8-K since July is the 2026-09-08 COO departure), so if the REO was sold in Q3 the market learns it tonight; if it was not, management will have to say 'still marketing' a third time, which is why the range is two-sided and the point estimate is small.
findings.independence: NPA, NPL and OREO figures from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001499422/000143774926023874/ex_970512.htm, 2026-07-20); 10-Q notes that nonaccrual SFR loans include $680k in foreclosure. The sweep row's 'where_to_look' named the same credit book independently. No second source on the REO's status.

findings.finding: EVP/COO Gary Fan left the bank on 2026-09-30 after a mutual decision on 2026-08-31 not to renew his agreement 'as part of the Bank's leadership transition plan', with severance of six months' base salary conditioned on a release (8-K filed 2026-09-08, Item 5.02): a small one-off expense accrued in Q3 on top of expenses already guided 'at the higher end' of $18-19M, and a third senior departure in 2026 after director Christopher Lin's April retirement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline turned on an expense one-off; efficiency ratio rose to 57.5% in Q2 and the stock moved -0.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K drew no coverage and no estimate revision; the amount (a few hundred thousand dollars, about a cent of EPS) is below the deadband on its own, and it is a one-off with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit.
findings.independence: Director Lin's April 2026 retirement 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001499422/000143774926011393/rbb20260403_8k.htm) is the only other turnover item; it is a different person and a different event.

findings.finding: Loan growth was guided to resume in H2 after loans HFI fell $15.8M in Q2: the Northern California team hired 2026-07-13 (John Curtis, ex-CEO of Bank of the Orient, plus two 25-year bankers, new SF Bay Area LPO) was said on the Q2 call to have a 'healthy pipeline', with CFO Hopkins guiding mid-single-digit annualised growth as payoffs slow and the CEO hoping for mid-to-high single digits in commercial; Q3 is the first quarter that can show it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loans shrank in Q2 and the stock moved -0.41%; loan growth has not been the line this stock trades on in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside what the company already guided, so it is mostly a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect; the Zacks revenue estimate of $34.07M already assumes some growth over Q2's ~$33M. The unpriced part is whether a brand-new team books anything in its first 80 days, which cuts both ways.
findings.independence: Press release on the company's own site plus the Q2 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/RBB/Q22026, 2026-07-21). Two documents, one claim.

findings.finding: The holder base turned over in H1 2026 without the price noticing: FJ Capital Management, a bank-specialist fund that held 1,766,083 shares (9.96%) at 2026-06-30-2025, reported 0 shares and 0% as of 2026-06-30 (13G/A Amendment 9), while Dimensional reported a new 5.3% position (902,290 shares, 13G, event date 2026-06-30), so a ~10% block was absorbed by passive money and the specialist seller is finished before this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline turned on holder changes; the stock rose 50% off its 52-week low through the period the block was being sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Already resolved and largely priced (the block was sold into the run-up); filed small because it removes one supply overhang into a thin name ($2.1M/day) and short interest is only 3.4% of float, so there is no natural seller positioned for a bad print either.
findings.independence: Dimensional 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001499422/000035420426000811/primary_doc.xml, event date 2026-06-30) is a separate filer and a separate document.

findings.finding: Peer tape read-through for the reaction function: Regions Financial (2026-10-16) printed NIM 3.68%, +2bp q/q, EPS $0.71 beating consensus on a revenue shortfall, and its shares rose 2.27%, so regional banks were being bought on an EPS beat last week after a month-long sell-off; RBB's bar ($0.57) sits below its Q2 run-rate ($0.59), which makes a headline beat the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RBB beat by $0.05 in Q2 ($0.59 vs ~$0.54) and moved -0.41%; beats have not reliably been bought on this name, which caps the size.
findings.why_not_priced: A proxy from a $150bn-asset Southeast bank with a hedging programme, filed as one; it says something about the sector's reaction function this week, nothing about RBB's own numbers.
findings.independence: Regions 3Q26 exhibit on EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001281761/000128176126000063/rf-2026930xexhibitx992.htm). No California or Asian-American peer has printed yet: Cathay 2026-10-21, Hanmi 2026-10-27, Preferred Bank not yet out.

outside_window.finding: Cathay General (the closest listed peer) reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-10-21 and Hanmi on 2026-10-27; their NIM and credit prints will reframe RBB after this window closes.

baseline_tension: The findings are net mildly positive on disclosed company items while the one large new fact (the Q3 rate shock) is negative and market-wide; the stock's -4.5% 20-day drift has absorbed some of it, there is no option skew to read, and short interest at 3.4% of float is not a mechanism either way, so nothing here cuts hard against the baseline and p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed is filed small): the Q3 rate-shock finding moved from -1.0 to -0.8; it stays filed because the AFS and time-deposit balances are the company's own numbers
Rule 5 (a proxy is sized as a proxy): the Regions reaction read-through moved from +0.2 to +0.15
Rule 6 (verify the bar): two agreeing sources at $0.57, so no cap applied; the stale Zacks/AAII figures were moved to rejected_candidates
Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the COO severance finding was already sized as a fraction and left at -0.1
Rules 1, 3, 7, 8, 9: nothing changed; p_up stays 52 and abs_move_pct 3.0
